ai.description: Keira’s Shrub Frog is a small, 20–23 mm amphibian. It features a brownish-grey dorsum with dark markings, a distinct white spot on the snout, and a pale venter with dark mottling.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes keirasabinae* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow patch on the posterior side of its thighs, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes keirasabinae* inhabits the high-altitude montane evergreen forests (shola) and adjacent grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically found above 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: Keira’s Shrub Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining hidden within dense vegetation during the day and emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes keirasabinae* undergoes direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. They breed during the monsoon, laying clutches of 10–15 eggs in arboreal nests.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes keirasabinae* is endemic to the high-altitude shola-grassland mosaics of the Western Ghats in Kerala, India, occurring at elevations above 2,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Raorchestes keirasabinae* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "tink" notes emitted from vegetation in evergreen forest habitats.
